question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle become a core owner of globally shared MCP declarations and their persistent cleanup ledger?
rationale: The change creates a new core authority over executable and remote MCP configuration while VISION.md prefers bundle-style plugins and the governing RFC remains open.

options.title: Defer to RFC
options.body: Keep the draft open until the RFC and prerequisite stack explicitly approve this core ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve core ownership
options.body: Accept the design after URL redaction, coexistence, upgrade, recovery, consent, and live-proof gates are complete.

options.title: Use plugin ownership
options.body: Move the lifecycle to bundle-style plugins or ClawHub if existing extension seams satisfy the capability.

recommendation.title: Defer to RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open until the RFC and prerequisite stack explicitly approve this core ownership boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned reviewer already evaluating the exact ownership and recovery contracts in this stack.
